canonical_statement: The work explores whether causal state-space dynamics placed before self-attention can supply sequential information so that a language model can operate without explicit positional encodings.
Each ZetaGPT block applies a causal state-space module before self-attention and then a feed-forward network, using three pre-normalized residual sub-layers.
The state-space module is designed so that its recurrent hidden state summarizes the ordered causal prefix before the representation reaches self-attention.
ZetaGPT instantiates the state-space component as a selective diagonal state-space module with input-dependent per-channel decay a_t = exp(-softplus(W_a x_t + b_a)).
The state-space input path uses a learned value projection, depthwise causal convolution, and SiLU nonlinearity, while a parallel projection supplies an output gate.
The instantiated recurrence updates h_t = a_t ⊙ h_{t-1} + (1-a_t) ⊙ v_t and produces y_t = W_o(h_t ⊙ SiLU(g_t)) + b_o.
The attention sub-layer uses standard causal multi-head attention and applies an input-dependent sigmoid gate to the concatenated attention output before the output projection.
ZetaGPT uses a byte-level BPE tokenizer initialized from 256 byte symbols and adds three special tokens: pad, eos, and unk.
A single tokenizer is trained on the pretraining corpus with 50,000 merge rules, giving a vocabulary size of 50,259 for all model configurations.
ZetaGPT-S uses 6 layers, 8 attention heads, d_model 384, head dimension 48, 4× MLP expansion, and 34.4M total parameters.
ZetaGPT-M uses 12 layers, 12 attention heads, d_model 768, head dimension 64, 4× MLP expansion, and 159.2M total parameters.
ZetaGPT-L uses 24 layers, 16 attention heads, d_model 1024, head dimension 64, 4× MLP expansion, and 479.9M total parameters.
The report states that context length is a training configuration rather than an architectural constraint because the model contains no explicit positional encoding.
Within the compact-model comparison assembled by the report, ZetaGPT is presented as the only listed State-Space-Attention language model without explicit positional encoding.

The end-to-end pipeline proceeds through data curation, BPE tokenizer training, pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, reward-model training, RLHF instruction-following tuning, and GRPO-based chain-of-thought reinforcement learning.
Language-model pretraining uses the WikiText-103 corpus.
Supervised instruction tuning uses the Alpaca-GPT4 instruction-following dataset, and the same instruction corpus is reused for reward-model training and RLHF.
Chain-of-thought reasoning training uses the GSM8K benchmark with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and no supervised chain-of-thought demonstrations.
All training stages use AdamW with β=(0.9,0.999), ε=1e-8, maximum global gradient norm 1.0, and cosine annealing to a minimum learning rate equal to one tenth of the peak rate.
Pretraining uses a learning rate of 2e-5 for 64,840 optimization steps.
Supervised fine-tuning uses a learning rate of 1e-6 for 2,342 optimization steps.
Reward-model training uses a learning rate of 1e-5 for 2,500 optimization steps.
RLHF uses a learning rate of 1e-6 for 3,251 optimization steps.
GRPO chain-of-thought reinforcement learning uses a learning rate of 1e-6 for 1,400 optimization steps.

Model checkpoints, training statistics, and state-space diagnostics are recorded every 200 optimization steps; unless otherwise specified, stages use batch size 16 and the model configuration’s pretraining context length.

canonical_statement: Memory horizons differentiated by layer during training: shallow layers retained the longest horizons, intermediate layers developed the shortest, and deeper layers converged to intermediate horizons.

The decay distribution evolved from a narrow initialization to a heterogeneous population with both short-memory and long-memory channels; long-memory channels with a>0.99 emerged after about 2,000 steps.
The pretraining corpus is intentionally modest in scale and cannot provide the linguistic diversity, world knowledge, or task coverage of contemporary models trained on much larger corpora.
The default 34.4M-parameter model is deliberately compact, and the report cautions that findings at this scale may not transfer directly to substantially larger language models.

Computational constraints limited pretraining contexts to 256, 512, and 1024 tokens across the three configurations, preventing a comprehensive empirical evaluation of long-context modeling and context-length extrapolation.
The authors conclude that recurrent state-space dynamics can provide position-aware representations before self-attention without explicit positional encodings.
The authors present ZetaGPT as the first open-source small language model without explicit positional encoding.
The authors present the project as a compact and reproducible reference implementation for developing, evaluating, and studying positional-encoding-free language models.
The report repeatedly identifies the project repository as https://github.com/roisincrtai/zetagpt and describes the implementation and end-to-end pipeline as fully open source.
